root_cause_label: Unauthorized Rounding in Manual Interpolation Implementation
one_sentence_failure_summary: When forced to reimplement interpolation without pandas, the agent introduced an unauthorized round(levels[i-1], 1) call that truncated high-precision interpolated water levels, causing a mismatch with the expected output despite otherwise correct logic.
t_err_evidence: In step 4, the agent rewrote the script using the csv module and included 'row[1] = str(round(levels[i-1], 1))' when writing interpolated values back — adding a rounding operation that the task specification never requested and that the oracle solution deliberately omits.
t_commit_evidence: At the end of step 4, the script ran successfully and overwrote all three CSV files with rounded values. Once the original files were overwritten with rounded data, the precision mismatch was locked in and could not be recovered without re-running the task from scratch.
trigger_explanation: The agent's overall plan and interpolation logic were correct, but when generating the manual CSV-based implementation, it added a spurious round() call that introduced an unauthorized transformation. No spec element called for rounding; this was a code-generation quality failure in the fallback implementation.
forewarning_evidence: Step 3 produced a ModuleNotFoundError for pandas, forcing the agent to pivot to a manual implementation. While this error does not directly predict the rounding bug, it created the condition (manual re-implementation) under which the bug was introduced.
